comments.text:
Second field occurrence, 2026-09-09, dev box. Raised P2 -> P1: this is no longer a one-off from a specific tooling path, it reproduces from ordinary repo drift.

WHAT HAPPENED
Three configured repos (claude-watch, herdr-bridge, mc, all under ~/dev) no longer existed on disk. beads_watch crash-looped 52+ times at ~2s intervals, taking down the five healthy repos (boxset, beads_watch, ctxhooks, scripts, skills) with them. Journal line, repeated forever:

  beads_watch: /home/goku/.config/beads_watch/config.json: repo "claude-watch": stat /home/goku/dev/claude-watch: no such file or directory

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE ORIGINAL REPORT SUGGESTS
The original case involved a mount-namespace quirk, which reads as exotic. This one did not: the directories were simply gone. On a multi-box setup that is routine drift, so the blast radius is 'any repo removed anywhere takes the whole tailnet daemon offline until a human notices'.

Detection is the quiet part. The unit sits in 'activating (auto-restart)', never 'failed', so it does not appear in systemctl --failed and does not trip unit-failure alerting. From a client the socket just never shows up. Nothing surfaces this except reading the journal directly.

HOW IT WAS RESOLVED IN THE FIELD (workaround, not a fix)
Removed the three dead entries from config.json and restarted; daemon came up clean, startup log confirmed repos=5. Original config backed up before edit. This is exactly the manual toil the bead proposes to eliminate.

RISKS FOR WHOEVER IMPLEMENTS
The obvious over-correction is making startup never fail. Do not. Config-shaped errors (typos, dupes, bad notify refs) must stay fatal, and zero servable repos must stay fatal - a silent daemon serving nothing is worse than a loud one. The regression guard for this is in the test plan.

Second risk: turning a loud failure quiet without a replacement signal. WARN + ok:false in GET /v1/repos is the floor; a notify event on healthy->unhealthy transition is worth considering so it reaches ntfy rather than dying in the journal.

CONFIRMED WHILE INVESTIGATING
The fix has strong in-codebase precedent. internal/server/server.go:182-211 already degrades per-repo at request time - repoStatus carries OK bool and Error string, and handleRepos records a failure rather than failing the listing. internal/events/events.go:64-65 documents the convention outright: 'Startup errors are config-shaped ...; per-repo trouble is logged.' Only internal/server/config.go:169-175 disagrees. This is an asymmetry to remove, not a new behaviour to invent.

SUCCESS CRITERIA
See the acceptance-criteria field, set on this bead as of this update.

title: Decide: scrub the real tailnet name from history (touches 4 bead bodies) or leave it
description:
## Background

The rewrite that produced the a44-io history replaced identities, trailers and
the old private-account GitHub URLs. Its first run did NOT replace the real
MagicDNS tailnet name (`<tailnet>.ts.net`; the literal string is recorded only
in /home/goku/dev/beads_watch-archive/.rewrite/replacements.txt, deliberately
not here), because doing so collided with a decision Goku had already made:
`.beads/` ships exactly as-is.

Where the name lived, as of the first rewrite's HEAD 6280c9d:

- `.beads/issues.jsonl` — 4 hits in bead bodies (bw-1tk, bw-mub, bw-hou: the
  whoami transcripts `actor: arch.<tailnet>.ts.net@arch`; bw-lt8: the ntfy
  host `ntfy.<tailnet>.ts.net`). 23 hits across historical versions of the
  file.
- `internal/tsidentity/tsidentity.go:39` — a comment giving the real FQDN as
  the example (1 hit; 1 in history). Docs and tests already used
  `example.ts.net`.
- README.md — 0 at HEAD (already moved to `example.ts.net`), 4 in history.

So the docs had been deliberately scrubbed, but the bead data and history
still carried the real name. Half a scrub.

## The question

Replace the real tailnet name with `example.ts.net` in HISTORY (which edits
the 4 bead bodies and every old blob of issues.jsonl), or accept the name in
public and only fix the tsidentity.go comment by hand?

What a MagicDNS tailnet name exposes: nothing resolvable or reachable from the
public internet; it is a fingerprint that could correlate this repo with any
other public mention of the same tailnet, and the whoami transcripts pair it
with node names (`arch`, `dev`, `pi`) and 100.x addresses.

## Options

A. Scrub in history, .beads included. Re-run the rewrite from the archive with
   one extra replacements.txt line, re-swap, force-push the private a44-io
   repo (no forks, nobody has cloned; free). Bead bodies of
   bw-1tk/bw-mub/bw-hou/bw-lt8 change wording; the DB is rebuilt from the
   scrubbed JSONL, which is the source of truth.

B. Leave history. Fix tsidentity.go:39 by hand (one word). Accept the name in
   4 closed beads and in old README blobs.

C. Scrub only non-.beads paths in history (filter-repo `--file-info-callback`
   keyed on filename). Keeps .beads byte-identical, but HEAD's issues.jsonl
   still shows the name in the public tree — the visible leak stays, which
   makes this the weakest option.

## Decision

Goku, 2026-09-16: **A**. "You can scrub it from everything including beads.
The jsonl is source of truth and it's free to backup and build an entire db
from scratch using it anytime with 1 command (why the jsonl is tracked in git
in the first place)."

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Switch tailscale serve from localhost TCP to the unix socket
description:
Currently served as: tailscale serve --bg --https=443 http://127.0.0.1:7717. The unix socket is preferred (mode 0600 shuts out other local users; localhost TCP does not). Serving a unix socket requires root, so this needs one operator command:

  sudo tailscale serve --https=443 off
  sudo tailscale serve --bg --https=443 unix:/run/user/1000/beads_watch.sock

Then restart the daemon without --listen so it binds the socket from config.
close_reason: Superseded by the caddy + systemd-socket-proxyd architecture (bw-ps7, Aug 26). tailscale serve no longer fronts the daemon on any box; caddy on pi proxies to the per-box proxyd bridge, which already forwards to the 0600 unix socket. The remaining concern from this bead — daemon reachable on localhost TCP by other local users — is moot: the daemon binds only the socket, and the bridge listens only on the tailscale IP. Direct-TCP identity forgery is tracked separately in bw-mub.

title: Pre-flip audit: re-run every rewrite gate plus tree/history/remote checks; record 'cleared for flip at <sha>'
description:
## Background

The rewrite's gates were run on 2026-09-16 (twice: the second pass added the
tailnet name) and passed: single identity `a44 <dev@a44.io>`, four tags
re-tagged, 0 hits for every leak pattern in messages and in every historical
blob, one Claude co-author line per Claude commit, refs/notes/sessions absent
from the remote. Every child of the epic commits on top of that. This bead is
the LAST thing before Goku runs
`gh repo edit a44-io/beads_watch --visibility public`: re-run every gate
against the tree and history as they are then, plus the checks the rewrite
deliberately left to the prepare phase.

The leak patterns themselves — the old account name, both old emails, the
old trailer formats, the real tailnet name — are written down in exactly one
place, `/home/goku/dev/beads_watch-archive/.rewrite/leak-patterns.txt` (one
`grep -E` pattern per line), which never leaves this box. This bead, and the
comment that records the run, must not spell any of them; a public bead that
quotes the pattern IS the leak. The first draft of this bead did exactly
that and had to be rewritten.

## Technical Approach

Run from /home/goku/dev/beads_watch after `git fetch origin` and confirming
`git status` is clean and `HEAD == origin/main`. Record every command and its
output in a comment on this bead (counts only — never the matched text).

    P=/home/goku/dev/beads_watch-archive/.rewrite/leak-patterns.txt

Hard-zero gates (any hit = stop, fix, re-run):

    git log --format='%an <%ae>|%cn <%ce>' | sort -u          # exactly one line, a44
    for t in $(git tag); do git cat-file tag $t | grep tagger; done   # only a44
    git log --format=%B | grep -cEf "$P"                      # 0 — messages
    git rev-list --objects --all | awk '{print $1}' | git cat-file --batch-check='%(objectname) %(objecttype)' \
      | awk '$2=="blob"{print $1}' | while read -r b; do git cat-file blob "$b"; done \
      | grep -cEf "$P"                                        # 0 — every historical blob
    git ls-remote origin | grep -c notes                        # 0
    gh api --paginate repos/a44-io/beads_watch/commits -q '.[].commit | .message, .author.email, .author.name, .committer.email, .committer.name' \
      | grep -cEf "$P"                                        # 0 — what GitHub actually serves
    grep -rnE 'bw\.dev\.a44\.io|beads-(arch|dev)\.dev\.a44\.io' --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=.beads --exclude-dir=dist .   # 0, or only inside a labelled fleet subsection
    grep -rn '923ce50' --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=.beads .   # 0 (pre-rewrite sha in README transcript)

Judgement gate:

    grep -rnoE '100\.(6[4-9]|[7-9][0-9]|1[0-2][0-9])\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=dist . | grep -v _test.go   # real 100.x addresses outside tests; README should be placeholders by now; bead text keeps them by decision

Presence gates:

    test -f LICENSE && gh repo view a44-io/beads_watch --json licenseInfo -q .licenseInfo.key   # mit
    grep -n '^## Install' README.md && grep -n 'releases/latest/download' README.md setup.sh   # the public one-liner exists in both
    gh release list --repo a44-io/beads_watch                   # at least one non-draft release with SHA256SUMS
    gh repo view a44-io/beads_watch --json visibility -q .visibility   # still PRIVATE when this runs

Then the checks a grep cannot do: read `git log --stat` from the commit that
filed this epic to HEAD and confirm no commit since the rewrite carries a
non-a44 identity or an old-style trailer (a commit made with hooks silenced
would); confirm the local `user.email` in the repo is still `dev@a44.io`
(`git config --local user.email`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every hard-zero gate prints 0 / the single expected line, pasted into a
  comment here with the HEAD sha it ran against.
- The leak-pattern gates print 0 and no matched text appears in the comment.
- All presence gates pass.
- A comment says "cleared for flip at <sha>" — and the flip itself is NOT
  done by this bead. Goku runs it.

## Test Plan

This bead is the test. Run it twice: once when all siblings are closed, and
again immediately before the flip if any commit landed in between.

## Considerations

- Blocked on every other child of the epic. The tailnet question is decided
  and applied (second rewrite pass, 2026-09-16); it stays a blocker only as
  the record of that decision.
- The gates that walk every blob take seconds on 32+ commits; no need to
  optimise.
- If a gate fails, do not patch around it: message HumbleSaffron (the
  omabeads session) or Goku with the output. The rewrite recipe in
  /home/goku/dev/beads_watch-archive/.rewrite/ can be re-run from the archive
  if history itself needs another pass — but after public exposure that is
  no longer free, which is why this runs BEFORE the flip.
acceptance_criteria: every hard-zero gate prints 0 / the single expected a44 line, pasted into a comment with the HEAD sha; the tailnet-name gates (name read from the archive's replacements.txt, never spelled) print 0; LICENSE, public Install one-liner, and a non-draft release exist; comment says 'cleared for flip at <sha>'; the flip itself is left to Goku
